---
title: "Validation data"
---

```{python}
import numpy as np, pandas as pd
import plotly.graph_objects as go
from plotly.subplots import make_subplots
from _lib import *
tr = traits()
spec = pd.read_csv(ROOT / "data/validation/spectra.csv")
order = sample_order()
```

The validation leaves come from
[`ashiklom/spectra_db`](https://github.com/ashiklom/spectra_db). LOPEX and
ANGERS are the only projects there with reflectance **and** transmittance plus
measured chlorophyll, carotenoids, water (EWT) and dry matter (LMA). The ten
leaves below span the trait ranges of those two libraries and include
senescent, white/variegated, sclerophyllous and very thin leaves. A synthetic
PROSPECT-D spectrum with known parameters and N(0, 0.005) noise is included as
a parameter-recovery check.

* LOPEX: Perkin-Elmer Lambda 19 with an integrating sphere, 400–2500 nm, 5 replicate
  R/T measurements per leaf (replicate 1 is fitted; all 5 are used on
  [Error models](error-models.qmd)).
* ANGERS: ASD FieldSpec with a leaf clip, 400–2450 nm, one R/T pair per leaf.
* EWT and LMA are already in g cm⁻², the units of PROSPECT's $C_w$ and $C_m$.
  Neither library measured anthocyanins.

```{python}
#| label: tbl-traits
#| tbl-cap: "Validation samples and measured traits."
t = tr.set_index("sample_id").loc[order].reset_index()
cols = ["sample_id", "project", "species", "role", "Cab", "Car", "Cw", "Cm"]
show_table(fmt_table(t[cols].rename(columns={
    "sample_id": "Sample", "project": "Project", "species": "Species", "role": "Why chosen",
    "Cab": "Cab (µg cm⁻²)", "Car": "Car (µg cm⁻²)", "Cw": "EWT (g cm⁻²)", "Cm": "LMA (g cm⁻²)"}), 3))
```

```{python}
#| label: fig-traitspace
#| fig-cap: "Measured traits of the validation set. Hover for sample details."
real = t[t["project"] != "synthetic"]
fig = make_subplots(rows=1, cols=2, horizontal_spacing=0.12)
for proj, sym in (("lopex", "circle"), ("angers", "diamond")):
    d = real[real["project"] == proj]
    hover = [f"{r.sample_id}<br>{r.species}<br>Cab {r.Cab} · Car {r.Car}<br>EWT {r.Cw} · LMA {r.Cm}"
             for r in d.itertuples()]
    fig.add_trace(go.Scatter(x=d["Cab"], y=d["Car"], mode="markers", name=proj.upper(),
                             marker=dict(symbol=sym, size=11, color=COLOR["stan" if proj == "lopex" else "pymc"],
                                         line=dict(color=SURFACE, width=2)),
                             text=hover, hovertemplate="%{text}<extra></extra>"), 1, 1)
    fig.add_trace(go.Scatter(x=d["Cm"], y=d["Cw"], mode="markers", name=proj.upper(), showlegend=False,
                             marker=dict(symbol=sym, size=11, color=COLOR["stan" if proj == "lopex" else "pymc"],
                                         line=dict(color=SURFACE, width=2)),
                             text=hover, hovertemplate="%{text}<extra></extra>"), 1, 2)
fig.update_xaxes(title_text="Chlorophyll a+b (µg cm⁻²)", row=1, col=1)
fig.update_yaxes(title_text="Carotenoids (µg cm⁻²)", row=1, col=1)
fig.update_xaxes(title_text="LMA (g cm⁻²)", row=1, col=2)
fig.update_yaxes(title_text="EWT (g cm⁻²)", row=1, col=2)
fig.update_layout(height=380, legend=dict(orientation="h", y=1.12, x=0))
show(fig)
```

## Spectra

```{python}
#| label: fig-spectra
#| fig-cap: "Reflectance (top) and transmittance (bottom) of each validation leaf. For LOPEX leaves, replicates 2–5 are shown in gray behind the fitted replicate 1. Choose a sample from the menu."
fig = make_subplots(rows=2, cols=1, shared_xaxes=True, vertical_spacing=0.07)
ntr = []
for i, sid in enumerate(order):
    d = spec[spec["sample_id"] == sid]
    n = 0
    for rep, g in d.groupby("replicate"):
        main = rep == 1
        color = COLOR["stan"] if main else "#c3c2b7"
        for row, q in ((1, "R"), (2, "T")):
            fig.add_trace(go.Scatter(
                x=g["wavelength"], y=g[q], mode="lines", visible=(i == 0),
                line=dict(color=color if row == 1 or not main else COLOR["pymc"], width=2 if main else 1),
                name=f"{q} replicate {rep}", showlegend=False,
                hovertemplate=f"%{{x}} nm<br>{q} = %{{y:.4f}}<extra>rep {rep}</extra>"), row, 1)
            n += 1
    ntr.append(n)
vis = lambda i: sum(([j == i] * ntr[j] for j in range(len(order))), [])
buttons = [dict(label=sample_label(s), method="update", args=[{"visible": vis(i)}]) for i, s in enumerate(order)]
fig.update_layout(updatemenus=[dict(buttons=buttons, x=0, y=1.13, xanchor="left")], height=560)
fig.update_yaxes(title_text="Reflectance", row=1, col=1)
fig.update_yaxes(title_text="Transmittance", row=2, col=1)
fig.update_xaxes(title_text="wavelength (nm)", row=2, col=1)
show(fig)
```

::: {.callout-note collapse="true"}
## Leaves considered and excluded

* `yang_pheno` (Harvard Forest seasonal series) has many young, anthocyanin-rich
  leaves, but its R/T files for the candidate red-oak leaf look scrambled: R
  jumps 0.02 → 0.10 → 0.03 → 0.34 across 550–800 nm, and the wavelength rows are
  out of order. It also has no EWT. `an03r0128` (highest anthocyanin
  reflectance index among the ANGERS leaves) is used instead.
* `lopex_11` and `lopex_66` look like dried leaves without pigment measurements.
* `processed-spec-data/*.rds` holds the same LOPEX/ANGERS data in an older R
  format; the `spectra_db` CSVY files were used instead.
:::
